query: Based on the segment disclosures and term definitions in their 2024 10-K filings, how do Intel and NVIDIA differ in the treatment of stock-based compensation expenses within their 'All Other' categories, and what does this reveal about their corporate expense allocation practices?
final_answer:
Based on the 2024 10-K filings, Intel and NVIDIA differ in the treatment of stock-based compensation expenses within their 'All Other' categories as follows:

- NVIDIA’s 'All Other' category explicitly includes stock-based compensation expense as one of the expenses that are not allocated to its reportable segments and are deemed enterprise in nature [1][3].
- Intel’s 'All Other' category comprises the results of other non-reportable segments (e.g., Altera, Mobileye) and does not include stock-based compensation. Instead, Intel lists share-based compensation among corporate operating expenses that are not allocated to any operating segment and that are kept separate from the 'All Other' category [2].

This difference reveals that NVIDIA aggregates enterprise-level expenses, including stock-based compensation, into the 'All Other' category for reconciliation purposes, while Intel treats such expenses as wholly unallocated corporate costs that are excluded from both its operating segments and its 'All Other' category. Both companies do not assign stock-based compensation to individual operating segments, but their presentation and location of these costs in segment reporting differ.

The Company measures deferred tax assets and liabilities using tax rates applicable to taxable income in effect for the years in which those tax assets are expected to be realized or settled and prov ides a v aluation allowance against deferred tax assets when it cannot conclude that it is more likely than not that some or all deferred tax assets will be realized. The assessment requires significant judgment and is performed in each of the applicable taxing jurisdictions. In addition, the Company recognizes tax benefits from uncertain tax positions only if it is more likely than not that they will be sustained, based on the technical merits of the positions, on examination by the jurisdictional tax authority. Interest and penalties related to income taxes are recorded within the Income tax prov ision (benefit) line in the Company's Consolidated Statements of Operations. The Company is subject to the Global Intangible Low T axed Income (GILTI) tax in the U.S. and recognizes deferred taxes for temporary basis differences that are expected to rev erse as GILTI tax in future years. ## Recently Issued Accounting Standard Updates Adopted In Nov ember 2023, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued Accounting Standard Update (ASU) 2023-07 Segment Reporting (T opic 280) Improv ements to Reportable Segment Disclosures to enhance disclosures about significant segment expenses.
